title: Accusative 7: Many Things Stay the Same
description: Inanimate plural nouns keep their nominative form in the accusative.
descriptionRussian: Неодушевлённые существительные во множественном числе не изменяются в винительном падеже.
intro: Plural nouns that name things behave like the masculine and neuter singulars you have already met: no change at all in the accusative. Plurals that name people and animals do change, but Russian holds that back until A2. So everything in this lesson is a thing, and everything in it keeps the form you already know.
rules: Inanimate plural nouns DO NOT change in the accusative. The form is identical to the nominative plural: журналы → журналы, книги → книги, окна → окна.
This rule covers all three genders in the plural, as long as the noun names things (not people or animals).
Animate plurals (друзья, студенты, собаки) follow a different rule and will be introduced at A2. For now, the lesson focuses on things only.
examples: Антон читает журналы. (Anton is reading magazines.) журналы → журналы, no change.
Маша любит книги. (Masha loves books.) книги → книги, no change.
Мы покупаем продукты. (We are buying groceries.) продукты → продукты, no change.
Лена открывает окна. (Lena is opening the windows.) окна → окна, no change.
Я вижу машины. (I see the cars.) машины → машины, no change.
Папа моет тарелки. (Dad is washing the plates.) тарелки → тарелки, no change.

tables.title: How the Plural Is Built (for recognition)

items.hint: Are журналы things or people? What does the inanimate plural rule say?
items.explanation: Журналы is the nominative plural of журнал (a thing). Inanimate plurals do not change in the accusative, so the form stays журналы.

items.hint: Книги are things. Apply the inanimate plural rule.
items.explanation: Книги is the nominative plural of книга. Since books are things, the accusative is identical to the nominative: книги.

items.hint: Продукты are things. What does the inanimate plural rule say?
items.explanation: Продукты is already plural (groceries). As inanimate, the accusative matches the nominative: мы покупаем продукты.

items.hint: Окна is neuter plural (-о → -а). Are windows things or people?
items.explanation: Окна is the plural of окно (-о → -а is the neuter plural pattern). Windows are things, so the accusative does not change.

items.hint: Flowers are things, not animate. What is the rule?
items.explanation: Цветы is the plural of цветок. Flowers are inanimate, so the accusative plural is identical to the nominative: цветы.

items.hint: Тарелки is the plural of тарелка. Things or people?
items.explanation: Тарелки is the nominative plural of тарелка (-а → -и after к). As inanimate, the accusative is the same form: тарелки.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Письма is the neuter plural of письмо (-о → -а). Inanimate plurals don't change in the accusative, so the form stays письма.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я каждый день читаю газет в библиотеке.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I read newspapers in the library every day.
errorCorrection.explanation: Газеты is an inanimate plural, so the accusative is identical to the nominative plural: газеты. Газет is the genitive plural, used in phrases like 'нет газет', not as a direct object.

errorCorrection.sentence: Соня покупает газет каждое утро у дома.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Sonya buys newspapers every morning near home.
errorCorrection.explanation: Газеты (newspapers) is an inanimate plural, so the accusative is identical to the nominative plural: газеты. Газет is the genitive plural ('много газет', 'a lot of newspapers'), used in counting and 'how many' constructions. For 'buys X' as a direct object, the plain plural form is required.

errorCorrection.sentence: Мы любим горам, особенно зимой в Альпах.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: We love the mountains, especially in winter in the Alps.
errorCorrection.explanation: Горы (mountains) is an inanimate plural, so the accusative is identical to the nominative plural: горы. Горам is the dative plural ('я иду к горам', 'I'm walking toward the mountains'), not a direct-object form. The inanimate plural rule is simple: the accusative always looks like the nominative.

errorCorrection.sentence: Она очень любит песнями о лете.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: She really loves songs about summer.
errorCorrection.explanation: Песни is an inanimate plural, so the accusative is identical to the nominative plural: песни. Песнями is the instrumental plural, not a direct-object form. After любит the plural keeps its nominative shape.

minimalPairs.explanation: Цветы is the inanimate plural accusative (no change from the nominative). Цветов is the genitive plural, used in sentences like 'У меня нет цветов' (I don't have flowers) or 'много цветов' (a lot of flowers).
Газеты is the inanimate plural accusative (= nominative plural). Газет is the genitive plural, used after words of quantity: 'много газет', 'нет газет'.
